commit 77df7b848e658ec8d907f14a700f94346f337f7b
Author: Michael Bowerman <michael.bowerman@liferay.com>
Date:   Fri Aug 13 15:58:20 2021 -0700

    LPS-136108 Create a new test class specifically to test the
    LayoutReferencesExportImportContentProcessor class.
    
    While we previously used the DefaultExportImportContentProcessorTest for
    this purpose, I believe it would be beneficial to create this new test
    class so we can create finer, more detailed tests that test all the many
    edge cases in the LayoutReferencesExportImportContentProcessor class.
    
    In the DefaultExportImportContentProcessorTest, the tests we run are at
    more of a "high" level. We run the content processor on a file that
    contains a large number of URLs, but we don't have a good mechanism to
    check the exact values of the resulting URLs. All we can do is check
    that the file contains or doesn't contain certain strings.
    
    In this new LayoutReferencesExportImportContentProcessor test class, we
    will create tests that consist of setting up Groups and Layouts in
    various ways, and then testing a single URL per test, to make sure that
    the resulting imported URL is as expected.
    
    In this first commit, we will just add one simple proof-of-concept test
    to test that a non-Liferay URL retains it's same values. We will add
    many more test cases in the next few commits.

    LPS-132215 users-admin-test: removes post-filtering fields from the assertion
    
    Field.COMPANY_ID, Field.ENTRY_CLASS_NAME, Field.ENTRY_CLASS_PK
    
    Since these three fields are only (automatically) added and useful in the
    post-filtering context. Once the post-filtering goes away, it is safe to assume
    that unless those fields are requested explicitly (as they are in
    UserIndexerIndexedFieldsByAssociationTest#testAssociationsThatIndexMoreFields),
    they will not be present in the returned documents.

Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>

    LPS-130359 Refactor to fix shared state bug
    
    As explained here:
    
        https://github.com/liferay-lima/liferay-portal/pull/1748#issuecomment-821050326
    
    `blogs-web` has two `<liferay-item-selector:image-selector>` taglibs in
    its `edit_entry.jsp`. Only the one the cover image one has a caption;
    the "small image" under "Configuration" does not.
    
    So, when we were firing events with `Liferay.fire()` from _either_
    selector, it would wind up hiding or showing the caption on the cover
    image. This is a bit of a smell anyway, because the image selector is
    supposed to be generic, but it was secretly coupled to `blogs-web` and
    was sending it a special event, and doing so in a non-specific way (ie.
    an event without an id, which meant that `blogs-web` couldn't
    distinguish between cover image changes and small image changes).
    
    The fix, then, is to go back to managing `image` state internally to the
    component, and only communicate with `blogs-web` for the case of the
    cover image (as identified by the `paramName` attribute). The bug is
    gone, although a bit of the smell remains (ie. the generic selector is
    still doing something secret/special for blogs). The alternative of
    making the secret "public" by adding an attribute to the taglib isn't
    much of an improvement, so we're going with this approach as it is
    minimal and it fixes the bug.
    
    It also means that this isn't an amazing showcase of `Liferay.State`,
    but it does at least show that you can use it to replace
    `Liferay.fire()`/`Liferay.on()`, and that you can adopt TS in an
    existing module even in the smallest of ways, if you want to. The state
    atom still contains the image info (`fileEntryId` and `src`), even
    though something smaller would have worked (eg. a boolean). It's still
    pretty small, and at least encodes some information that might be useful
    when debugging.
    
    Test plan:
    
    1. Before this commit (and on `master`). See that adding or removing an
       image to the cover image selector or the small image selector causes
       the caption to appear disappear.
    2. After this commit, see that adding/removing works; the caption only
       shows/hides in response to cover image changes. Small and cover
       images can be added/removed without affecting the other.

commit 4bfac73f9fcea03d2c3f6ff02f1b944df0ab78b9
Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>
Date:   Tue Apr 13 19:28:05 2021 +0200

    LPS-130359 Port cover image events to use Liferay.State API
    
    -   We had a mess with the types before this PR[0]. The `propTypes` say
        that `fileEntryId` is required and must be a string, but in the
        component we were using `0` (the number) to mean something special
        (no image), and `'-1'` (the string) to mean something else (upload
        in progress).
    
    -   Likewise, we were firing events that included image data, but none
        of the listeners were actually doing anything with it (ie.
        `_showCaption()` and `_removeCaption()` in `blogs-web` don't take
        any parameters.
    
    -   So, in this commit I make the types uniform: `fileEntryId` is typed
        as `string` and we always set a string. To make the special meaning
        of `'0'` obvious, I created a named constant for it
        (`STR_NULL_IMAGE_FILE_ENTRY_ID`), following the local pattern. Now,
        I could export that for use in `blogs-web`, and probably will, but
        for now I am just hard-coding `'0'` over there; will do that
        tomorrow.
    
    -   Instead of having a `useState` that manages the `image` object, I
        replaced that with `useLiferayState`, replacing my earlier
        `State.write()` calls. This is good because it means we communicate
        just by setting the state, as opposed to setting the local state
        _and_ updating the global store. But we should note some
        architectural weirdness here: we are kind of abusing global state
        here to have these two projects communicating with one another; you
        can only have one blogs screen active at a time, and one image
        selector, which is to say, this works in a non-colliding way only
        because we happen to have a UI that doesn't show more than one thing
        at a time.
    
    -   One way the weirdness manifests itself is that the state isn't
        "really" global. We pass in `fileEntryId` to the image selector, and
        we use `useEffect()` to write that into global storage on the first
        render. In reality, the responsibility for seeding the global store
        should happen higher up (maybe in the page.jsp), but that just
        highlights the weirdness of it all... we're rendering a single image
        selector in a way that depends on global state and only works
        because we effectively "guarantee" that it's a singleton.
    
    Removed killable events as part of this, as advocated here:
    
        https://github.com/liferay-frontend/liferay-portal/pull/970#discussion_r614141386
    
    Test plan:
    
    1. In blogs, add a cover image via drag an drop. Delete it. Change it
       and select a new file. Try this over and over again in different
       orders with the JS console open and see no errors.
    
    2. Verify that the "small image" selector that appears under
       configuration still works as before.
    
    3. Create a commerce catalog and add a product to it. Add an image using
       the image selector there and see it work as before.
    
    [0]: https://github.com/liferay-frontend/liferay-portal/pull/970

    LPS-129801 Update to `@liferay/npm-scripts` v42.0.0
    
    This is the one that manages our TS config for us, as explained here:
    
        https://github.com/liferay/liferay-frontend-projects/releases/tag/npm-scripts%2Fv42.0.0
    
    Lots of details explained in:
    
    - https://github.com/liferay/liferay-frontend-projects/pull/478
    - https://github.com/liferay-frontend/liferay-portal/pull/942
    
    But the high-level summary can be found here:
    
    https://github.com/liferay/liferay-frontend-projects/blob/f5917d11d60d5b17ac3845e247e48ac87136ed22/projects/npm-tools/packages/npm-scripts/src/typescript/README.md
    
    In short, the TypeScript compiler (`tsc`) can support our modular
    project layout by using a feature called "project references". This
    means each project needs only worry about its own types (stored in the
    "types/" folder), so gets the safety of global type-checking across
    liferay-portal, but also the fast builds that come with building each
    project in isolation. In order to get the full benefit of editor
    integration with the type-system (eg. autocomplete, inline
    documentation, "go-to-definition" etc), we must manage and commit the
    "tsconfig.json" files in the root of each project. All of this is
    abstracted away inside `@liferay/npm-scripts` and up-to-date-ness is
    enforced during `ci:test:sf`.
    
    Test plan:
    
    1. Run `yarn run liferay-npm-scripts types` and see it prime all the
       config files.
    2. Run `yarn run build` in TS-using modules and see them build. They
       emit a warning when out of date.
    3. When clean, see that `yarn run build` emits no warning because
       everything is up-to-date.
    4. See `ci:test:sf` correctly fail/pass on the test PR, linked above.

    LPS-129801 Port a couple of hook tests to TS
    
    Showing my work as separate steps here to show how to do this kind of
    port incrementally. For additional context, see the PRs here:
    
    - https://github.com/liferay-frontend/liferay-portal/pull/925
    - https://github.com/liferay-frontend/liferay-portal/pull/942
    
    This commit ports a couple of tests to TS. Observations:
    
    - We need to pull in the same `.eslintrc.js` config as we're using in
      `frontend-js-state-web`, otherwise ESLint will complain about using
      `React` before its defined. This is an obvious candidate for baking
      into our default ESLint config (either in `@liferay/eslint-config`
      itself, our `@liferay/npm-scripts` base, or higher up in the repo).
    - Tests have JSX in them, which means we need to use the "tsx" file
      extension, and update our jest.config.js accordingly.
    - Likewise, we need `"jsx": "react"` in our tsconfig.json in order to
      support JSX. I'd say this is something that we can bake in to
      `@liferay/npm-scripts`.
    - We need types for react-dom. Adding them locally in this commit for
      now as a hack, seeing as we already have a Source Formatter exclusion
      configured for frontend-js-react-web (normally we don't allow
      devDependencies to be added). Need to decide whether to bake this in
      to `@liferay/npm-scripts` like almost all other devDependencies, or
      whether we're happy to keep it here to "tie it" together with the
      actual version of `react`/`react-dom` that we're using (note: as it
      is, the type definitions are heard of the concrete version of React
      that we're using).
    - Refined the types in `useStateSafe`, because continuing the port to TS
      revealed some gaps.

commit 986ba2ee5b0aa5ff96b0a63b0b2f7c291b3357f7
Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>

    LPS-129801 Move useLiferayState into frontend-js-react-web
    
    This requires us to set up TS compilation in frontend-js-react-web.
    
    Obviously, all of this is horridly manual at this point and just serves
    as proof that you _can_ require TS from another module and have it work
    ie.:
    
    - Build process in either module picks up type errors.
    - Test runner in either module runs both JS and TS.
    - LSP-powered editor features (eg. display of type info, errors) works.
    
    I'm going to upload this just as a proof of concept and continue to
    investigate more ergonomic ways of configuring this. The main pain point
    is that ambient types don't get picked up automatically, which is why I
    added that "triple-slash directive" to force their inclusion:
    
        https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/triple-slash-directives.html
    
    Other things tried that didn't work included adding the other project
    under the `typeRoots` config, and renaming the type folder to match the
    pattern that TS seems to expect for named scope packages (eg.
    `liferay__frontend-js-state-web`); I also tried just using the named
    scope literally, but that didn't work either.
    
    Next thing I'll be investigating is leveraging project references in
    some way:
    
        https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/project-references.html

commit 7931612bc9012c41a96bb3b424f7e210652aa327
Author: Julien Castelain <julien.castelain@liferay.com>
Date:   Fri Feb 19 14:28:55 2021 +0100

    LPS-127832 Manage boolean dynamic attributes
    
    In this change, we're changing the `buildDynamicAttributes` method of
    the [InlineUtil](https://github.com/liferay/liferay-portal/blob/7985dd55f78d0b4e4960d1b8b07158787e32d29f/util-taglib/src/com/liferay/taglib/util/InlineUtil.java) class to handle boolean attributes.
    
    According to the [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#boolean-attribute), the presence of
    a boolean attribute on an element represents the "true" value, and the
    absence of the attribute represents the "false" value, but the values
    "true" and "false" are not allowed on boolean attributes. To represent a
    false value, the attribute has to be omitted altogether.
    
    If a dynamic attribute is one of the 25 available boolean attributes (see [here](https://meiert.com/en/blog/boolean-attributes-of-html/))
    and it's value is "false", we omit writting it and if it's value is
    "true" we replace it with the name of the attribute.
    
    **Test plan**
    - Fetch this branch
    - Deploy the `util-taglib` module
    - Add this code to a jsp, for example [buttons.jsp](https://github.com/liferay/liferay-portal/blob/85f66220f377144c4cf025be77a04c763a9f04b2/modules/apps/frontend-taglib/frontend-taglib-clay-sample-web/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/partials/buttons.jsp)
    
    ```jsp
    <clay:button disabled="<%= true %>" label="Disabled" />
    <clay:button disabled="<%= false %>" label="Enabled" />
    ```
    
    - Assert that it renders
        - A button with the `disabled` attribute (and no value)
        - A button without a `disabled` attribute

    LPS-121719 Use master version of svg4everybody.js
    
    The project is pretty much unmaintained at this point: the last release
    was about 3 years ago, although the `master` branch has commits as
    recently as April this year (2020).
    
    So, we take a snapshot of the source by grabbing the LICENSE.md and the
    lib/svg4everybody.js source file as of current HEAD of `master`, and
    basically concatenating them:
    
    - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonathantneal/svg4everybody/8bd711049ba3faefb8285ca70c63a67efc35636c/LICENSE.md
    - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jonathantneal/svg4everybody/8bd711049ba3faefb8285ca70c63a67efc35636c/lib/svg4everybody.js
    
    The project is simple, 0 dependencies, and 1 source file. We can ignore
    the Gruntfile based UMD build that the project uses and just compile
    this with `@liferay/npm-scripts`.
    
    Changes made to the source:
    
    -   Wrap whole thing in an IIFE and assign to `window.svg4everybody`.
    -   Format source.
    -   Fix lints:
    
            143:10  error  'svg4everybody' is defined but never used.  no-unused-vars
            153:6  error  'LEGACY_SUPPORT' is not defined.  no-undef
            187:13  error  'LEGACY_SUPPORT' is not defined.  no-undef
            245:9  error  'LEGACY_SUPPORT' is not defined.  no-undef
            302:9  error  Expected object keys to be in natural ascending order. 'id' should be before 'svg'.  sort-keys
    
        Note that we can just delete all the sections guarded by
        `LEGACY_SUPPORT` because we never used the legacy build.
    
    Because the build is simpler now, we can strip out most of the
    `build.gradle` file.
    
    Test plan:
    
    In portal-ext.properties, set:
    
        cdn.dynamic.resources.enabled=false
    
    (This is the only way to inject svg4everybody, unless you are on IE,
    which you no longer can be on `master`).
    
    Load portal and see script successfully retrieved from:
    
        /o/frontend-js-svg4everybody-web/index.js
    
    See transpiled source looks right:
    
        https://gist.github.com/wincent/5c61c838e0b8e3445e552c167cd9f2ef
    
    And that `svg4everybody()` exists in the console.

commit eaf642681a2bc725d6652590f508a5270306ab46
Author: Chema Balsas <jose.balsas@liferay.com>
Date:   Thu Oct 15 08:59:35 2020 +0200

    LPS-122191 Removes unnecessary FlashMagicBytes checks
    
    The FlashMagicBytesUtil checks were added to prevent [CSRF attack using
    uploaded flash files](https://issues.liferay.com/browse/LPS-52121). We
    will no longer support Adobe Flash in DXP 7.4.
    
    Adobe will stop providing security fixes for the platform in December
    2020 and browsers will prevent any content from running past that date.
    
    `FlashMagicBytesUtil` uses a `PushbackInputStream` to read the first bytes
    of an `InputStream` and then simply rewinds it and provides means to
    access it. That means that when removing the usage, we can simply use
    the original `InputStream` to keep the same behaviour.
    
    To avoid a major kernel breaking change, we're simply deprecating both
    `FlashMagicBytesUtil` and `FlashMagicBytesUtilTest` instead of deleting
    them.

commit e0a32153f22ddc068587e2d6a5f51eaba7d987ce
Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>
Date:   Mon Oct 26 14:25:16 2020 +0100

    LPS-121753 Fix test failure in remote-app-client-js
    
    Tests were dying with:
    
        TypeError: _index.__LIFERAY_REMOTE_APP_SDK__.Client is not a constructor
    
    For much the same reason as we saw and fixed in "LPS-121753 Don't use
    object concise methods for AUI component constructors" some commits
    back; we can't use object concise methods as constructor functions, and
    we were previously able to do it only because our Babel config turned
    them into something other than concise functions.
    
    So this commit fixes that by hoisting the concise method out to the
    top level (which is nice in any case because it reduces indentation
    by one level), but note that even though that is enough to unbreak
    the tests, I am *also* applying the same kind of config that I did in
    analytics-client-js, I don't think we officially want the SDK to drop
    IE support (seeing as it was "included" in 7.3, even though we still
    haven't published it to the CDN).

commit 2c75cdcf8834a2275841cf12100972e31603ca82
Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>
Date:   Mon Jul 13 15:17:42 2020 +0200

    LPS-116988 Update react-dnd to v11.1.1
    
    Matches the upgrade that we prepared for the Commerce folks on 7.1.x:
    
    - https://github.com/wincent/liferay-portal-ee/pull/9
    - https://github.com/wincent/liferay-portal-ee/pull/10
    
    What's going on here:
    
    -  Bump version numbers from 10.0.1 to 11.1.1; there are later versions
       out now, but they bring nothing of value and given that we've seen
       11.1.1 working on 7.1.x, I want to stay in line with that.
    
    -  Adjust `HTML5Backend` imports; this is the breaking change in the v10
       to v11 update: previously it was a default export but now it is a
       named export.
    
    -  Configure `frontend-js-react-web` to get `domain` from
       `frontend-js-node-shims`; this is because `domain` is `require()`-ed
       here, which would cause the loader to throw an error:
    
       https://github.com/react-dnd/asap/blob/b6bebeb7342/src/node/raw.ts#L87
    
    -  Configure `frontend-js-react-web` to get `process` from
       `frontend-js-node-shims`; this is because — the horror —
       `@react-dnd/asap` expects it to be a global:
    
       https://github.com/react-dnd/asap/blob/b6bebeb7342/src/node/asap.ts#L24
    
       We set up this global in the index of `frontend-js-react-web`, to be
       sure that it is set by any client that may conceivably need it.
    
       If we don't do this, drag-and-drop works fine, but when you try to
       navigate away from a page, we hit the above line and an error is
       thrown, breaking the transition and spewing out a bunch of red crap
       into the console.
    
    -  Note that only `frontend-js-react-web` needs these imports
       configured. Other modules that use `react-dnd` get it from
       `frontend-js-react-web` and don't need to meddle with the transitive
       dependencies themselves; at least, in my testing of a couple of
       places (`segments-web` and `layout-content-page-editor-web`) I didn't
       see any loader errors.
    
    -  Drop forced resolution of `dnd-core`. Previously, we were doing that
       in order to avoid running into all the above problems with `domain`
       and friends. By using an older version of `dnd-core`, we avoided the
       problematic `@react-dnd/asap` fork of the `asap` package, which came
       into react-dnd in v10.0.2:
    
       https://github.com/react-dnd/react-dnd/commit/ada65550b75
    
       We can no longer use this resolution because resolutions are a very
       limited tool: they allow us to control what gets installed at build
       time but they do not influence what happens at runtime. In other
       words, if a package like `dnd-core` has a dependency with a range
       like "^3.0.0", and we want to pin to version "3.0.1" or something
       else compatible, then resolutions work well. But as soon as the range
       changes to "^4.0.0" we can no longer useful pin to "3.0.1", even if
       we know it to be compatible: Yarn will install the version we
       require, but at runtime the loader will blow up because the
       dependency graph says that `dnd-core` wants "^4.0.0" and we won't
       have it due to the resolution.
    
    One thought: it would be nice if we could force the various pieces of
    our module loading system (bundler, loader, registry) to work with
    react-dnd without these hacks, but that is probably beyond the scope of
    this task. If you look at their package.json, you can see how they've
    tried to make it work via `"main"` and `"browser"` fields, but I'm not
    even sure they're doing it right...
    
    https://github.com/react-dnd/asap/blob/b6bebeb7342/package.json#L15-L26
    
    Test plan: Test drag and drop in two apps (`segments-web` and
    `layout-content-page-editor-web`); see it working with no errors in
    console. Run all JS unit tests in repo.

Author: Julien Castelain <julien.castelain@liferay.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 16 12:12:28 2020 +0200

    LPS-113561 Avoid Liferay.provide in portal-reports-engine-console-web
    
    As part of [LPS-113561](https://issues.liferay.com/browse/LPS-113561) we
    eventually want to deprecate the `Liferay.provide` function, the
    `<portlet:namespace />testDatabaseConnection` function is now directly declared,
    on the `window` object and it's AUI dependencies have been removed.
    
    An interesting detail about this change is that in my case the
    `<portlet:namespace />testDababaseConnection` function was failing
    because of a missing AUI dependency as can be seen
    [here](https://git.io/Jf5Cf).
    
    To test this change:
    
    - Make sure you're running DXP:
      run `ant setup-profile-dxp` before running `ant all`
    - Navigate to "Configuration > Reports Admin"
    - Click on the "Sources" tab
    - Click on the "+" button to add a new source
    - Enter a name
    - Enter a value for "JDBC Driver Class Name"
      (com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver)
    - Enter a value for "JDBC URL"
      (jdbc:mysql://localhost/lportal_master?useUnicode=true&characterEncoding=UTF-8&serverTimezone=UTC)
    - Enter a value for "JDBC User Name"

    LPS-113561 Avoid unnecessary call to `Liferay.provide` in asset-list-web
    
    As part of [LPS-113561](https://issues.liferay.com/browse/LPS-113561),
    we eventually want to deprecated the `Liferay.provide` function.
    
    The code here was using it twice to expose functions on the `window`
    object: one of those was internal only, so didn't need to be exposed,
    and the other doesn't have any dependencies (which is the main reason
    you would use `Liferay.provide` in the first place), so can just be
    defined manually.
    
    Additionally, we avoid the same group being added twice in the "scope"
    section.
    
    Tested as follows:
    
    - Navigate to "Content and Data" > "Collections"
    - From the "New" drop down menu, select "Dynamic Selection"
    - Give it the name you want and click on the "Save" button
    - Scroll down to the "Scope" section
    - Click on the "Select" button
    - Choose "Global"
    - Click on the "Select" button again and choose "Global" again
    
    As a result the "Global" item should be present only once in the "scope"
    section.
    
    With the devtools open, locate the input element who's `id`
    attribute is `_com_liferay_asset_list_web_portlet_AssetListPortlet_groupIds` and
    confirm that it's `value` attribute contains several numbers (ids), none
    of which are duplicated.

    Applying this with the METHOD scope will ensure that data is deleted
    after every test method run. This makes the @DeleteAfterTestRun

    to be sure that they control how many users there are.

commit 0e24e13fe934233ac381d480e7ab7fc633493da4
Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>
Date:   Wed Feb 26 11:08:37 2020 +0100

    LPS-109341 Fix bugs in fixRedundantCommaInsideArray
    
    I was looking at this check because it tries to remove the trailing
    commas in JS arrays/objects added by Prettier; see sample test run:
    
    https://github.com/brianchandotcom/liferay-portal/pull/85253#issuecomment-590984955
    
    In resolving this, discovered a couple of bugs and made the following
    changes:
    
    -   Fix bug where the pattern was only catching commas in indented columns
        (because it was looking for `,\n\t+}` instead of `,\n\t*}`.  This was
        causing it to remove the trailing comma from `array1` but not `array2`:
    
        ```
        <%
        if (1) {
            int array1 = {
                1,
                2,
            };
        }
    
        int array2 = {
            1,
            2,
        };
        %>
        ```
    
        Solution is updating the pattern.
    
    -   Fix bug where the pattern was being applied indiscriminately to all
        source text (ie. plain HTML, not just Java source). This would cause
        the following HTML to be incorrectly mutated:
    
        ```
        <h1>Look at my code sample</h1>
    
        <pre>
            <code>
                const aTest = {
                    foo: 1,
                    bar: 2,
                };
            </code>
        </pre>
        ```
    
        Solution is adding an `isJavaSource()` check, which conveniently
        also means that we won't conflict with Prettier any more when it
        comes to formatting the JS source inside JSP.
    
    -   Moved `fixRedundantCommaInsideArray` from `BaseLineBreakCheck` to
        `JSPLineBreakCheck` because that is the only place it is used.

Author: Greg Hurrell <greg.hurrell@liferay.com>
Date:   Thu Oct 17 14:33:56 2019 +0200

    LPS-98032 Apply manual ESLint fixes
    
    Address these issues:
    
    https://gist.github.com/wincent/69535729aa70f916fda87f189ef291ab
    
    Some of them were false positives, likely caused by a bug in ESLint,
    where it things variables declared with `for (const a in b)` to be
    unused; in all of those cases except one I was able to switch to
    `Object.keys` instead, which is better than `in` anyway because it
    obviates the need to do an `hasOwnProperty()` check. The exception was a
    `FormData` instance for which I am not sure whether IE will do the right
    thing, so I left that one as it was and added a suppression.
    
    The move of the `jest.mock()` call is safe because Jest transparently
    hoists such calls up to the top of the module anyway via Babel at
    runtime. Tests still pass in that module.

       that means we can use them across all of our React projects. At the
       same time we updated from the versions of the libraries that we were
       already using in segments-web.
    
    2. We turn automated source formatting back on for frontend files.
    
    Tested like this:
    
    On this branch, see that `ant format-source-current-branch` only checks
    the changed files:
    
         [exec] > Task :yarnFormatModules
         [exec] yarn run v1.13.0
         [exec] $ liferay-npm-scripts fix --production false
         [exec] Prettier checked 21 files, found 0 files with problems
         [exec]
         [exec] ESLint checked 20 files, found 0 errors, found 0 warnings
         [exec] Done in 6.27s.
         [exec]
         [exec] BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s
         [exec] 1 actionable task: 1 executed
    
    See that `ant format-source-all` checks everything:
    
         [exec] $ liferay-npm-scripts fix --production false
         [exec] Prettier checked 1450 files, found 0 files with problems
         [exec]
         [exec] /Users/greghurrell/code/portal/liferay-portal/modules/apps/hello-soy/hello-soy-navigation-web/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/Navigation.es.js
         [exec]   18:8  warning  'Footer' is defined but never used  no-unused-vars
         [exec]   19:8  warning  'Header' is defined but never used  no-unused-vars
         [exec]
         [exec] /Users/greghurrell/code/portal/liferay-portal/modules/apps/hello-soy/hello-soy-web/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/View.es.js
         [exec]   18:8  warning  'Footer' is defined but never used  no-unused-vars
         [exec]   19:8  warning  'Header' is defined but never used  no-unused-vars
         [exec]
         [exec] ✖ 4 problems (0 errors, 4 warnings)
         [exec]
         [exec] ESLint checked 551 files, found 0 errors, found 4 warnings
         [exec] Done in 24.10s.
    
    Note that there is a file on "master" which currently has a formatting
    error, so expect CI to complain about that. The fix is currently at:
    
    https://github.com/brianchandotcom/liferay-portal/pull/75689
    
    Also, the fix for those last 4 (non-fatal) warnings is at:
    
    https://github.com/brianchandotcom/liferay-portal/pull/75696
    
    How the partial formatting works: we pass an environment variable
    containing the upstream branch name (called "git.working.branch.name" in
    portal-impl/build.xml) so that `liferay-npm-scripts` can compute the
    merge base and get the changed file list. I initially was going to take
    the file list in via an environment variable, but I suspect that the
    maximum size limits on Windows (a little over 8k characters) would be
    insufficient in this repo where we have many files and the average path
    length is 120 characters, which would mean we could run out of space
    after only around 68 files). The alternative version is described in
    detail at:
    
    https://github.com/liferay/liferay-npm-tools/pull/165

    LPS-63898 In case of XYZ does not live with XYZTest in the same package, the previous main class resolving logic is going to break. In those cases, developer must feed the main class for assertion by using appendAssertClasses(). CodeCoverageAssertor will still try to resolve main class in case it does live in the same package as the test class. But this resolving must be done via a brand new URLClassLoader, it is not allowed to load the classes being tested via the current literal classloader before "_DYNAMICALLY_INSTRUMENT_METHOD.invoke(null, includes, _excludes);". Becuase in case those classes have static initializers, loading it via current literal classloader before instrument will cause coverage lost, as those static initialzers will never run again with int the current literal classloader.

    LPS-59167 Fix CI build-test.xml: "mapping values are not allowed here"
    
    Java properties file format special markers:
    
    \n --> property value embeds a newline and continues in the same line
    trailing \ --> property value concatenates next line without separation
    
    Combining the two markers:
    
    trailing \n\ --> property value embeds a newline, continues next line
    
    Therefore it's possible to write a properties file with very long
    multiline property values (such as JSON or YML snippets) by having
    several lines ending with a trailing \n\ for each value.
    
    
    ```
    [junit] [PACLTestSuite]00:02:47,335 ERROR
    [main][com_liferay_portal_search:96]
    [com.liferay.portal.search.internal.SearchEngineHelperImpl(14)] The
    addSearchEngineConfigurator method has thrown an exception
    [junit] SettingsException[Failed to load settings from
    [cluster.routing.allocation.disk.threshold_enabled:
    false,cluster.service.slow_task_logging_threshold: 600s,
    index.indexing.slowlog.threshold.index.warn:
    600s,index.search.slowlog.threshold.fetch.warn:
    600s,index.search.slowlog.threshold.query.warn:
    600s,monitor.jvm.gc.old.warn: 600s,monitor.jvm.gc.young.warn: 600s]];
    nested: ScannerException[null; mapping values are not allowed here;  in
    'reader', line 1, column 101:
        [junit]      ... vice.slow_task_logging_threshold: 600s,
    index.indexing.slowlog.t ...
        [junit]                                          ^];
        [junit]     at
    org.elasticsearch.common.settings.Settings$Builder.loadFromSource(Settings.java:1052)
    ```

    LPS-53250 Refactor *PersistenceTest to not depend on *ModelImpl. As in modules, test module does not have dependency on impl module. And also the unconditional cast is not guaranteed safe, as the service module might actually return a different type of impl class. By using reflection, it does not give the guarantee either, but at least we can get rid of the dependency, and as long as the service module returned type follows the same methods organizing, it will just work not matter what the concrete type actually is. So over all this change gives us more flexibility when running tests in modules, without introducing any new issues.

Date:   Tue Nov 11 17:23:14 2014 +0100

    LPS-51191 make DLApp*ServiceTest pass
    
    The file version to use when changing status will need to be fetched
    before or after the call to update/revert depending on the
    circumstances. This is so because inside de update/revert method an auto
    check in/out may be made, changing the version under the hood. To handle
    this we use FileVersionRefernece, which is responsible of reading the
    correct file version at the correct moment. Note that once we move the
    check in code into a capability (in a couple of commits), this class
    won't be needed anymore and will be removed.
    
    Also, we need to refresh the FileEntry before returning it. Otherwise,
    the version changes won't be propagated correctly.
